         6       Duarte Day in the State of New York.

         7                  ACTING PRESIDENT MORAHAN:

         8       Senator Schneiderman, on the resolution.

         9                  SENATOR SCHNEIDERMAN:    Thank you,

        10       Mr. President.  On the resolution.

        11                  Today is the day that we are

        12       resolving to commemorate the birth of Juan

        13       Pablo Duarte.

        14                  And it's a very important, I think,

        15       resolution as we start this new cycle to

        16       celebrate people who were warriors in the

        17       cause of democracy.  We take for granted the

        18       right to vote here, the right to have a

        19       democratic government.  But we're reminded by

        20       our friends and family from the Dominican

        21       Republic that that right is not easily won.

        22                  So we celebrate today a great

        23       fighter in the cause of liberty, and we're

        24       honored to be joined today by some of the

        25       consuls from the Dominican Consulate, who are

         1       here to celebrate with us.  It's an important

         2       day for all who believe in the cause of

         3       freedom and democracy.

         4                  And I hope that as our education

         5       system continues to improve, more of our

         6       children will learn of the historic struggle

         7       and the heroic struggles of Juan Pablo Duarte

         8       and the Duartianos.

         9                  And if I may, Mr. President,

        10       (Comments on the Resolution spoken in

        11       Spanish].

        12                  So felicidades, bienvenidos, and

        13       it's great that we're here to celebrate

        14       together.

        15                  Thank you very much, Mr. President.

        20       you, Mr. President.  I rise to explain my

        22                  I will be voting in support of this

        23       legislation, but I would like to do a codicil

        25                  This legislation is part of the


                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

                                                        220



         1       Child Sexual Assault Reform Act.  And for the

         2       last four years, of the six that I've been

         3       here in the State Senate, I have been making a

         4       vigorous attempt to pass this bill in its

         5       entirety.  The only part of me that's pleased

         6       to see at least that incrementally this bill

         7       is getting passed.

         8                  My concern is that if this bill was

         9       really good in its essence, why this bill

        10       wasn't passed in its entirety, particularly

        11       because we have had so many people who are

        12       looking forward to the passage of this bill so

        13       that we can talk about prosecution of people

        14       who have committed sexual assaults against

        15       children.  And we also have been looking hard

        16       and long for a resolution to the statute of

        17       limitations.

        18                  In working on this bill, I have

        19       developed it based upon the recommendations of

        20       the Suffolk County Supreme Court special grand

        21       jury and their investigation of clergy abuse

        22       in the Diocese of Rockville Centre; I've

        23       consulted with the Bronx, Westchester, and

        24       Rensselaer district attorneys and the New York

        25       State Trial Lawyers, all of whom have worked


                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910

                                                        221



         1       to help to fine-tune and to hone this bill

         2       into something that would be crafted to

         3       respond to the needs of our constituents.

         4                  And while the elimination of the

         5       statute of limitations was passed by Senator

         6       Skelos last year, and while he has established

         7       a five-year statute of limitations for civil

         8       lawsuits for crimes of rape in the first

         9       degree and criminal sexual act and aggravated

        10       sexual abuse first degree or course of sexual

        11       conduct against a child in the first degree,

        12       and while it has created mandatory reporting

        13       of child abuse, including sexual assault,

        14       there are pieces that are still missing in

        15       this bill.

        16                  And one of those is the creation of

        17       the crime of endangering the welfare of a

        18       child in the first degree, which is an

        19       E felony and, secondly, a misdemeanor degree,

        20       and adds them to the list of specified

        21       premeditated crimes.

        22                  It also fails to extend the statute

        23       of limitations for hindering the prosecution

        24       of a sexual offense.  It fails to add clergy

        25       to the list of mandated reporters without --


                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1       with the exception of confessional, the

         2       confessional.  And it further does not allow

         3       for a two-year window for this course of

         4       action to take place.

         5                  I would hope, Senator Skelos, in

         6       your review of this bill, that as you pick and

         7       choose to pass legislation along lines that

         8       I'm not clear about that you will continue to

         9       pursue these aspects of the bill so that the

        10       people and particularly the children who have

        11       been abused in this state have a decent and

        12       appropriate recourse.

        13                  Thank you, Mr. President.
